hip-gluteal--gluteal.name: Gluteal muscles
hip-gluteal--gluteal.summary: The large muscles of the buttock. They extend, abduct and rotate the hip and keep the pelvis level when you stand on one leg.

hip-gluteal--deep-rotators.name: Deep lateral rotators
hip-gluteal--deep-rotators.summary: Short muscles behind the hip joint that turn the thigh outward and hold the femoral head in the socket.

hip-gluteal--iliopsoas.name: Iliopsoas
hip-gluteal--iliopsoas.summary: The main hip flexor: psoas major and iliacus, which share a tendon to the lesser trochanter.

thigh-knee--anterior.name: Anterior thigh
thigh-knee--anterior.summary: Knee extensors (the quadriceps) and sartorius. All supplied by the femoral nerve.

thigh-knee--medial.name: Medial thigh
thigh-knee--medial.summary: Hip adductors. Mostly supplied by the obturator nerve.

thigh-knee--hamstrings.name: Hamstrings
thigh-knee--hamstrings.summary: Hip extensors and knee flexors. Supplied by the sciatic nerve.

leg-ankle--anterior.name: Anterior leg
leg-ankle--anterior.summary: Dorsiflexors and toe extensors. Supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

leg-ankle--lateral.name: Lateral leg
leg-ankle--lateral.summary: The evertors of the foot. Supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.

leg-ankle--superficial-calf.name: Superficial calf
leg-ankle--superficial-calf.summary: The plantarflexors that form the calf and join the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.

leg-ankle--deep-calf.name: Deep calf
leg-ankle--deep-calf.summary: Popliteus and the three long muscles that pass behind the medial malleolus (Tom, Dick and Harry: tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, flexor hallucis longus).

foot-area--dorsum.name: Dorsum of the foot
foot-area--dorsum.summary: The two short extensors on the top of the foot.

foot-area--sole-1.name: Sole, first layer
foot-area--sole-1.summary: The most superficial layer, just under the plantar aponeurosis.

foot-area--sole-2.name: Sole, second layer
foot-area--sole-2.summary: Muscles attached to the long flexor tendons.

foot-area--sole-3.name: Sole, third layer
foot-area--sole-3.summary: Short muscles of the big and little toes.

foot-area--sole-4.name: Sole, fourth layer
foot-area--sole-4.summary: The interossei, between the metatarsals. Dorsal interossei abduct and plantar interossei adduct the toes (DAB and PAD).

gluteus-maximus.origin: Outer ilium behind the posterior gluteal line, the back of the sacrum and coccyx, and the sacrotuberous ligament.
gluteus-maximus.insertion: Most fibres into the iliotibial tract; the deep lower fibres into the gluteal tuberosity of the femur.
gluteus-maximus.actionText: Extends the hip, especially from a flexed position (rising from a chair, climbing stairs), and rotates it laterally. Through the iliotibial tract it helps steady the extended knee.
gluteus-maximus.note: Weak gluteus maximus shows as difficulty rising from sitting and a backward trunk lurch when walking.

gluteus-medius.origin: Outer surface of the ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines.
gluteus-medius.insertion: Lateral surface of the greater trochanter.
gluteus-medius.actionText: Abducts the hip and its anterior fibres rotate it medially. Most importantly, it keeps the pelvis level when the opposite foot is off the ground.
gluteus-medius.note: Weakness gives a positive Trendelenburg sign: the pelvis drops on the unsupported side.

gluteus-minimus.origin: Outer surface of the ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines.
gluteus-minimus.insertion: Anterior surface of the greater trochanter.
gluteus-minimus.actionText: Abducts and medially rotates the hip; with gluteus medius it keeps the pelvis level in single-leg stance.

tensor-fasciae-latae.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine and the front of the iliac crest.
tensor-fasciae-latae.insertion: The iliotibial tract, which attaches to the lateral condyle of the tibia (Gerdy's tubercle).
tensor-fasciae-latae.actionText: Flexes, abducts and medially rotates the hip, and tenses the iliotibial tract to steady the extended knee.

piriformis.origin: Anterior surface of the sacrum (roughly S2–S4) and the sacrotuberous ligament.
piriformis.insertion: Upper border of the greater trochanter.
piriformis.actionText: Laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip.
piriformis.note: The landmark of the gluteal region: the sciatic nerve usually exits the pelvis just below it.

superior-gemellus.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, by blending with the obturator internus tendon.
superior-gemellus.actionText: Laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip.

obturator-internus.origin: Inner (pelvic) surface of the obturator membrane and the bone around it.
obturator-internus.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, after turning around the lesser sciatic notch.
obturator-internus.actionText: Laterally rotates the extended hip, abducts the flexed hip and holds the femoral head in the acetabulum.

inferior-gemellus.origin: Upper part of the ischial tuberosity.
inferior-gemellus.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, by blending with the obturator internus tendon.
inferior-gemellus.actionText: Laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip.

quadratus-femoris.origin: Lateral border of the ischial tuberosity.
quadratus-femoris.insertion: Quadrate tubercle on the intertrochanteric crest of the femur.
quadratus-femoris.actionText: Laterally rotates the hip and holds the femoral head in the acetabulum.

psoas-major.origin: Sides of the bodies of T12–L5 and the discs between them, and the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae.
psoas-major.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur, through a tendon shared with iliacus.
psoas-major.actionText: Flexes the hip. With the thigh fixed it flexes the trunk (sitting up from lying) and bends the lumbar spine to the same side.
psoas-major.note: A tight psoas pulls the lumbar spine into extension and the pelvis into anterior tilt.

iliacus.origin: Iliac fossa, inner lip of the iliac crest and the ala of the sacrum.
iliacus.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur, through the psoas tendon.
iliacus.actionText: Flexes the hip, and with psoas major flexes the trunk on the fixed thigh.

rectus-femoris.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine (straight head) and the ilium just above the acetabulum (reflected head).
rectus-femoris.insertion: Base of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
rectus-femoris.actionText: Extends the knee and flexes the hip.
rectus-femoris.note: The only quadriceps muscle that crosses the hip, so it is a two-joint muscle.

vastus-lateralis.origin: Greater trochanter, upper intertrochanteric line and the lateral lip of the linea aspera.
vastus-lateralis.originShort: Greater trochanter and lateral linea aspera
vastus-lateralis.insertion: Base and lateral border of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
vastus-lateralis.note: The largest part of the quadriceps.

vastus-medialis.origin: Intertrochanteric line and the medial lip of the linea aspera.
vastus-medialis.insertion: Base and medial border of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
vastus-medialis.actionText: Extends the knee. Its lowest fibres (often called VMO) pull the patella medially and help it track in the femoral groove.

vastus-intermedius.origin: Anterior and lateral surfaces of the femoral shaft.
vastus-intermedius.insertion: Base of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
vastus-intermedius.note: Lies deep to rectus femoris, directly on the femur.

sartorius.insertion: Upper medial surface of the tibia, as part of the pes anserinus.
sartorius.actionText: Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip, and flexes the knee: together, the cross-legged sitting position.
sartorius.note: The longest muscle in the body.

pectineus.origin: Pectineal line (pecten) of the superior pubic ramus.
pectineus.insertion: Pectineal line of the femur, just below the lesser trochanter.
pectineus.nerveNote: Femoral nerve (sometimes also the obturator nerve)

adductor-longus.origin: Body of the pubis, just below the pubic crest.
adductor-longus.insertion: Middle third of the linea aspera.
adductor-longus.actionText: Adducts the hip and helps flex it.
adductor-longus.note: Its tendon is the one most often strained in a groin injury.

adductor-brevis.origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
adductor-brevis.originShort: Body and inferior ramus of pubis
adductor-brevis.insertion: Pectineal line and the upper part of the linea aspera.
adductor-brevis.actionText: Adducts the hip and helps flex it.

adductor-magnus.origin: Adductor part: inferior pubic ramus and ischial ramus. Hamstring part: ischial tuberosity.
adductor-magnus.insertion: Adductor part: gluteal tuberosity, linea aspera and medial supracondylar line. Hamstring part: adductor tubercle.
adductor-magnus.nerveNote: Adductor part: obturator nerve. Hamstring part: tibial division of the sciatic nerve
adductor-magnus.actionText: Adducts the hip. The adductor part also flexes it; the hamstring part extends it.
adductor-magnus.note: A muscle with two nerves because it is really two muscles fused together.

adductor-minimus.name: Adductor minimus
adductor-minimus.origin: Inferior pubic ramus (the upper part of adductor magnus).
adductor-minimus.insertion: Upper linea aspera, below the gluteal tuberosity.
adductor-minimus.actionText: Adducts and laterally rotates the hip.
adductor-minimus.note: Often described as the uppermost part of adductor magnus rather than a separate muscle.

gracilis.origin: Body of the pubis and the inferior pubic ramus.
gracilis.originShort: Body and inferior ramus of pubis
gracilis.insertion: Upper medial surface of the tibia, as part of the pes anserinus.
gracilis.actionText: Adducts the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the leg when the knee is bent.
gracilis.note: The only adductor that crosses the knee.

obturator-externus.origin: Outer surface of the obturator membrane and the bone around the obturator foramen.
obturator-externus.actionText: Laterally rotates the hip and holds the femoral head in the acetabulum.

semitendinosus.insertion: Upper medial surface of the tibia, as part of the pes anserinus.
semitendinosus.nerveNote: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
semitendinosus.actionText: Extends the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the leg when the knee is bent.
semitendinosus.note: Its long tendon makes up the lower half of the muscle.

semimembranosus.insertion: Posterior surface of the medial tibial condyle.
semimembranosus.nerveNote: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
semimembranosus.actionText: Extends the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the leg when the knee is bent.
semimembranosus.note: Lies deep to semitendinosus. Its flat upper tendon gives it its name.

long-head-of-biceps-femoris.name: Biceps femoris, long head
long-head-of-biceps-femoris.insertion: Lateral side of the head of the fibula.
long-head-of-biceps-femoris.nerveNote: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
long-head-of-biceps-femoris.actionText: Extends the hip, flexes the knee and laterally rotates the leg when the knee is bent.

short-head-of-biceps-femoris.name: Biceps femoris, short head
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.origin: Lateral lip of the linea aspera and the lateral supracondylar line of the femur.
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.insertion: Lateral side of the head of the fibula, shared with the long head.
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.nerveNote: Common fibular division of the sciatic nerve
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.actionText: Flexes the knee and laterally rotates the leg when the knee is bent.
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.note: The only hamstring part that does not cross the hip and is not supplied by the tibial division. A classic exam question.

tibialis-anterior.origin: Lateral condyle and upper half of the lateral surface of the tibia, and the interosseous membrane.
tibialis-anterior.insertion: Medial and underside of the medial cuneiform and the base of the first metatarsal.
tibialis-anterior.actionText: Dorsiflexes the ankle and inverts the foot. It lowers the forefoot gently after heel strike.
tibialis-anterior.note: Weakness causes foot drop: a slapping foot or a high-stepping gait.

extensor-hallucis-longus.origin: Middle of the anterior surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
extensor-hallucis-longus.insertion: Dorsal base of the distal phalanx of the big toe.
extensor-hallucis-longus.actionText: Extends the big toe and dorsiflexes the ankle.
extensor-hallucis-longus.note: Testing big-toe extension is the classic check of the L5 myotome.

extensor-digitorum-longus.origin: Lateral condyle of the tibia, upper three-quarters of the anterior fibula and the interosseous membrane.
extensor-digitorum-longus.originShort: Lateral tibial condyle and anterior fibula
extensor-digitorum-longus.insertion: Middle and distal phalanges of toes 2–5, through the extensor expansions.
extensor-digitorum-longus.actionText: Extends toes 2–5 and dorsiflexes the ankle.

fibularis-tertius.origin: Lower third of the anterior surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
fibularis-tertius.insertion: Dorsum of the base of the fifth metatarsal.
fibularis-tertius.actionText: Dorsiflexes the ankle and everts the foot.

fibularis-longus.origin: Head and upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
fibularis-longus.insertion: Base of the first metatarsal and the medial cuneiform, reached by crossing under the sole.
fibularis-longus.actionText: Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes the ankle; supports the arches of the foot.

fibularis-brevis.origin: Lower two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
fibularis-brevis.insertion: Tuberosity on the base of the fifth metatarsal.
fibularis-brevis.actionText: Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes the ankle.
fibularis-brevis.note: An inversion sprain can pull off the tuberosity it attaches to (an avulsion fracture of the fifth metatarsal).

medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.name: Gastrocnemius, medial head
medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.origin: Posterior surface of the femur just above the medial condyle.
medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus through the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.actionText: Plantarflexes the ankle and helps flex the knee. Strongest at plantarflexion when the knee is straight.
medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.note: Crosses both the knee and the ankle. The Achilles reflex tests S1.

lateral-head-of-gastrocnemius.name: Gastrocnemius, lateral head
lateral-head-of-gastrocnemius.origin: Lateral surface of the lateral femoral condyle.
lateral-head-of-gastrocnemius.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus through the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
lateral-head-of-gastrocnemius.actionText: Plantarflexes the ankle and helps flex the knee.

soleus.origin: Back of the head and upper fibula, the soleal line and medial border of the tibia.
soleus.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus through the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
soleus.actionText: Plantarflexes the ankle whatever the knee position. Its steady tone stops you swaying forward when standing.
soleus.note: Does not cross the knee, so it is the plantarflexor that works with the knee bent.

plantaris.origin: Lateral supracondylar line of the femur and the oblique popliteal ligament.
plantaris.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus, alongside the calcaneal tendon.
plantaris.actionText: Weakly assists plantarflexion and knee flexion.
plantaris.note: Small and often absent; its long tendon is used for grafts.

popliteus.origin: Lateral surface of the lateral femoral condyle, with attachment to the lateral meniscus.
popliteus.insertion: Posterior surface of the tibia above the soleal line.
popliteus.actionText: Unlocks the fully extended knee by rotating the femur laterally on the planted tibia, then helps flex it.
popliteus.note: Called the key that unlocks the knee.

tibialis-posterior.origin: Interosseous membrane and the adjoining posterior surfaces of the tibia and fibula.
tibialis-posterior.originShort: Posterior tibia, fibula and interosseous membrane
tibialis-posterior.insertion: Tuberosity of the navicular, plus the cuneiforms, cuboid and bases of metatarsals 2–4.
tibialis-posterior.actionText: Inverts the foot and plantarflexes the ankle; the main dynamic support of the medial arch.
tibialis-posterior.note: Tendon dysfunction is a common cause of adult-acquired flat foot.

flexor-digitorum-longus.origin: Posterior surface of the tibia below the soleal line.
flexor-digitorum-longus.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of toes 2–5.
flexor-digitorum-longus.actionText: Flexes toes 2–5, plantarflexes the ankle and supports the longitudinal arch.

flexor-hallucis-longus.origin: Lower two-thirds of the posterior fibula and the interosseous membrane.
flexor-hallucis-longus.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the big toe.
flexor-hallucis-longus.actionText: Flexes the big toe, plantarflexes the ankle and supports the medial arch. Gives the final push-off in walking.

extensor-digitorum-brevis.origin: Upper lateral surface of the calcaneus.

extensor-hallucis-brevis.origin: Upper lateral surface of the calcaneus.
extensor-hallucis-brevis.insertion: Dorsal base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
extensor-hallucis-brevis.actionText: Extends the big toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

abductor-hallucis.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity, the flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis.
abductor-hallucis.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
abductor-hallucis.insertionShort: Proximal phalanx of big toe, medial side
abductor-hallucis.actionText: Abducts and flexes the big toe; supports the medial arch.

flexor-digitorum-brevis.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity and the plantar aponeurosis.
flexor-digitorum-brevis.insertion: Both sides of the middle phalanges of toes 2–5.
flexor-digitorum-brevis.actionText: Flexes toes 2–5 at the proximal interphalangeal joints.

abductor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.name: Abductor digiti minimi (foot)
abductor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.origin: Medial and lateral processes of the calcaneal tuberosity and the plantar aponeurosis.
abductor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe.
abductor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.actionText: Abducts and flexes the fifth toe; supports the lateral arch.

quadratus-plantae.origin: Medial and lateral surfaces of the underside of the calcaneus.
quadratus-plantae.insertion: Posterolateral edge of the flexor digitorum longus tendon.
quadratus-plantae.actionText: Straightens the oblique pull of flexor digitorum longus, helping it flex the toes.

lumbrical-muscles-of-foot.name: Lumbricals (foot)
lumbrical-muscles-of-foot.insertion: Medial sides of the extensor expansions of toes 2–5.
lumbrical-muscles-of-foot.nerveNote: First lumbrical: medial plantar nerve. Lateral three: lateral plantar nerve
lumbrical-muscles-of-foot.actionText: Flex the metatarsophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints of toes 2–5.

medial-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.name: Flexor hallucis brevis, medial head
medial-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.origin: Underside of the cuboid and lateral cuneiform.
medial-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe, through the medial sesamoid.
medial-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.actionText: Flexes the big toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

lateral-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.name: Flexor hallucis brevis, lateral head
lateral-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.origin: Underside of the cuboid and lateral cuneiform.
lateral-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe, through the lateral sesamoid.
lateral-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.actionText: Flexes the big toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

oblique-head-of-adductor-hallucis.name: Adductor hallucis, oblique head
oblique-head-of-adductor-hallucis.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
oblique-head-of-adductor-hallucis.insertionShort: Proximal phalanx of big toe, lateral side
oblique-head-of-adductor-hallucis.actionText: Adducts the big toe and supports the transverse arch.

transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.name: Adductor hallucis, transverse head
transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.origin: Plantar ligaments of the metatarsophalangeal joints of toes 3–5.
transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.insertionShort: Proximal phalanx of big toe, lateral side
transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.actionText: Adducts the big toe and supports the transverse arch.

flexor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.name: Flexor digiti minimi (foot)
flexor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.insertion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe.
flexor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.actionText: Flexes the fifth toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

opponens-digiti-minimi-of-foot.name: Opponens digiti minimi (foot)
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-foot.origin: Long plantar ligament near the base of the fifth metatarsal.
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-foot.insertion: Lateral border of the fifth metatarsal.
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-foot.actionText: Draws the fifth metatarsal toward the sole. Often absent and usually counted as part of flexor digiti minimi.

plantar-interossei-muscles.name: Plantar interossei
plantar-interossei-muscles.origin: Bases and medial sides of metatarsals 3–5.
plantar-interossei-muscles.insertion: Medial sides of the bases of the proximal phalanges of toes 3–5.
plantar-interossei-muscles.actionText: Adduct toes 3–5 toward the second toe (PAD) and flex the metatarsophalangeal joints.

dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-foot.name: Dorsal interossei (foot)
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-foot.origin: Adjacent sides of metatarsals 1–5 (four muscles, each with two heads).
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-foot.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges: the first on the medial side of toe 2, the others on the lateral sides of toes 2–4.
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-foot.actionText: Abduct toes 2–4 away from the line of the second toe (DAB) and flex the metatarsophalangeal joints.
